newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes $3 a tonne up, crude recovers.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes $3 a tonne up, crude recovers.

text.p: IPE December gas oil futures closed $3.00 a tonne higher in light volume and dealers said the contract came off the day's high after the Jan/Feb spread came under a bit of pressure.
December gas oil closed at $222.75 a tonne, off the intra-day high of $224.50 a tonne. Traders said the contract held well despite a weak performance by NYMEX heating oil, which was 27 cents off.
"Jan/Feb came under a bit of pressure, having been steady all day at $7.25. There is not a great deal going on and heat drifted off under reasonably light volume.
"It's a typical Tuesday night and the market is very cautious ahead of the APIs," a gas oil broker said.
The American Petroleum Institute is due to release weekly U.S. stock figures with analysts divided as to whether there will be a draw or a build in distillates stocks.
January crude futures also recovered after falling to a low of $23.35 a barrel shortly after remarks by an Iraqi official that he thought crude exports could resume by next week.
Front-month Brent was pulled off the lows by NYMEX and was at 1752 GMT trading seven cents lower at $23.55 a barrel.
Traders said speculation over the timing of Iraqi crude exports was having little effect on market moves.
"The position that we're taking is that we'll believe it when we see it," said a dealer.
